title: Certificate-Type Charge on an Owner Auto Policy Reinstatement with Lapse — Service Desk Q&A
content:
**Rule.** On a reinstatement with lapse of an Owner Auto Policy term, a certificate-type charge is added to the reinstatement fee, set by the type of the certificate backed by the term. The certificate is a Financial Responsibility Filings (SR-22 / FR-44) filing, read as it stood on the reinstatement effective date, and selected as follows:
- the certificate entered first with status filed, when its filed date is on or before the reinstatement effective date;
- otherwise, the certificate entered first with status cancellation filed, when its filed date is on or before that date.

A certificate filed after the reinstatement effective date does not change the reading.

| Type of that certificate | Charge added |
|---|---|
| Owner-operator certificate | 3.00 |
| Owner certificate | 2.00 |
| Operator certificate, or no such certificate | nothing |

**Questions the rule answers.**
- *Which certificate is read when one is filed and another has status cancellation filed?* The filed one, when its filed date is on or before the reinstatement effective date.
- *Does an operator certificate add a charge?* No. Only owner-operator and owner certificates add one.
- *Hypothetically, if the selected certificate is an SR-22 Owner-Operator Certificate, what is added?* 3.00.
